meta.source_title: Traverse Performance Characterization for the Mars Science Laboratory Rover (Heverly et al.; Journal of Field Robotics 30(6), 2013)
meta.grousers: chevron grousers at 15 deg spacing, 7.5 mm radial height (Sec 3)
meta.gravity_g: 1 (Earth test; vehicle mass chosen for Mars weight)
meta.vehicle: Scarecrow (Mars weight MSL mobility test rover, 340 kg, six wheel rocker bogie)
meta.soil: Dumont Dunes aeolian dune sand, Mojave Desert, California (natural, cohesionless)
meta.figure_or_table: Section 6.3 text (cubic fit to Figure 12 data)
meta.comparability_note: Third order polynomial slip(%) = c0 + c1 s + c2 s^2 + c3 s^3 with s the slope in deg, coefficients printed in Sec 6.3 (c0 = 26.197, c1 = -8.849, c2 = 1.281, c3 = -0.034), evaluated here at whole degrees inside the stated validity range of about 4 to 21 deg. Below 4 deg the paper expects nearly constant slip of about 10 percent; above 21 deg slip in excess of 90 percent and embedding. Fit residuals are not reported; the scatter in Figure 12 (curve heverly2013_fig12_scarecrow_dumont) shows the spread. Same vehicle and sand caveats as that curve. load_per_wheel_N derived here from Table I Earth weight 3329 N divided by 6 wheels.
